t: #2283 Check if Number Has Equal Digit Count and Digit Value
o: For each index i, digit i must occur exactly num[i] times in the string. In "1210": digit 0 occurs once (matches num[0]='1'), digit 1 occurs twice (num[1]='2'), digit 2 once (num[2]='1'), digit 3 zero times (num[3]='0') → true. In "030" digit 0 should occur 0 times but occurs twice → false. With n ≤ 10, just count all digits and compare.
k: Count occurrences of each digit 0–9, then verify count[i] == num[i] for every index i.
Digits larger than n−1 cannot appear as indices, but they still affect counts of indices that reference them.

a.i: Tally digit frequencies with a size-10 array, then check each index i against its required count num[i]. Any mismatch returns false.
s: Build cnt[10] from the characters of num.
For i in 0..n-1, if cnt[i] != num[i] - '0', return false.
a.t: O(n) — one pass to count, one pass to verify.

w: Single approach is sufficient. Pitfall: comparing character codes instead of numeric values ('0' vs 0), and remembering that counts of digits ≥ n are irrelevant except as demanded amounts. Follow-up: what if num could be huge (streamed)? Still O(n) time, O(1) space with the same counting idea.
